questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to write poems that rhyme and are easy to learn
How poetry helps emotionally and explains big ideas
Why poetry is no longer taught at many schools
The life and work of a famous English poet
questions.why: They discuss the positive power of poetry: healing emotions and explaining global issues like climate change.

questions.q: How does Neil feel about poetry?
options: He writes a new poem every week for his family
He thinks poetry is really only for children
He goes to open mic nights in London quite often
He'd like to read more, but doesn't get it
questions.why: Neil says he would love to read more poetry, but he just doesn't get it.

Learning to swim in the sea as an adult
Her own long time in hospital last year
Painting a picture of her garden
questions.why: Maria says she wrote it about a friend she loves dearly, who suffered a stroke.

questions.q: What does Maria say about going to an open mic night?
options: It makes her feel too nervous to perform
It's mainly for professional, published poets
It can make life feel better, even on a bad day
It's usually too noisy to hear the poems
questions.why: She says even if you're having a bad day, life can feel so much better after one.

questions.q: What does the group Hot Poets do?
options: Teach poetry to young children in primary schools
Publish books of love poems by new writers
Organise climate protests in big cities
Hear science talks, then perform poems about them
questions.why: They go to meetings like the UN Climate Conference, listen to papers, then write and perform poems.

questions.q: What is Liv Torc's poem based on?
options: A study about biodiversity
A true murder case at sea
A trip to see whales
Her childhood by the sea
questions.why: Pippa says Liv's poem is based on a study into biodiversity.

questions.q: According to Liv, what is the problem with how science is communicated?
options: Scientists refuse to talk to the public about it
There are not enough scientific studies being done
The jargon is hard to follow, so people lose interest
Science is only published in English journals
questions.why: She says the jargon is hard to understand and the science is impenetrable, 'so it's instantly a turn-off'.

questions.q: What does scientist Kat Bruce suggest about Liv's poem?
options: It made her research sound much too simple
It says what she wished she could say herself
It contained some serious scientific mistakes
She didn't really understand what it meant
questions.why: Kat says it still gives her goosebumps and is 'everything that I wish I could say'.
